newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close mixed, some banks in demand.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close mixed, some banks in demand.

text.p: Italian shares closed mixed on Tuesday with telecoms mostly in retreat as investors took profits but selected banks were in strong demand, led by San Paolo and Banco di Napoli.

The all-share Mibtel index closed 0.22 percent lower at 13,774 while the blue chip Mib30 also finished 0.22 percent down at 20,979. A firm lira and a well supported bonds market also helped underpin equities.
Stet and Telecom Italia, set to merge shortly, were the worst hit among telecom stocks, losing 1.34 percent to 10,050 lire and 1.17 percent to 5,580 lire respectively.
ENI was hit by profit-taking, dipping 0.32 percent but held its ground above 10,000 lire, closing at 10,018 lire.

Among the banks, Ambroveneto, which made most of the running last week, shed 2.6 percent to 5,993 lire while Credito Italiano was still in favour, ending the day 3.33 percent higher at 3,564 lire. San Paolo finished 5.05 percent higher at 13,936 lire.
Insurers were again out of favour, Generali 1.52 percent lower at 31,204 lire with RAS easing 2.24 percent to 14,285 lire.
Investors are concerned about the ability of Italian insurers to compete profitably as the market opens up to rivals from abroad.
